text:
Maya: Quick sync — dropped a sketch for a long-term 'regional strata' plan that ties routing policies, multi-region failover, and a customer onramp for tenant isolation. Link: https://redwood.internal/notes/regional-strata-draft 

Maya: TL;DR: define 3 launch lanes (soft-isolation, guarded-affinity, full-residency). Each lane has gating criteria, default fallback policies, and cost/econ signals. Need product + infra buy-in on gates + SLA phasing.

Ravi: skimmed — love the lane idea. Can we map lanes to Dedicated vs Hosted behaviour? e.g., guarded-affinity = Hosted w/ regional affinity, full-residency = Dedicated/Private.

Sam: yep. also important: define what rollback looks like across lanes. we had a messy customer cutover last quarter because rollback was region-by-region. suggest an explicit evacuation plan per lane.

Lina: +1 on evacuation plan. also we should surface a simple acceptance rubric for Sales/CE to use (3 items max) before we promise region-residency.

Maya: proposing acceptance rubric: 1) perf: p95 < 250ms baseline, 2) observability: route tracing + audit logs enabled, 3) econ: estimated >90% of traffic served within target SLO w/in committed capacity. Thoughts?

Jesse: those are reasonable. add a fourth optional: customer data residency attestation for regulated verticals. Could be gating for full-residency.

Ravi: +1. operational ask: infra needs a policy DSL that can express "preferred-region, failover-region, tenant-quota" and an override for Dedicated customers. can infra team own the DSL + runtime?

Sam: infra can prototype a minimal DSL but we need product to own semantics + testing harness (canary prompt sets, latency cohorts).

Maya: noted. On prioritization: propose we treat customers asking for strict residency as "high touch" sales-opportunity that triggers Dedicated/Private onboarding; general affinity requests go to guarded-affinity lane. This will help scope platform work.

Lina: Suggest we create two launch milestones: M1 (guarded-affinity alpha) and M2 (full-residency pilot). M1 focus = routing primitives + observability; M2 = residency enforcement + billing/contracting flow.

Ravi: timebox M1 to 8 weeks? Need a small cross-functional squad. Ops-Bot: @ops-bot created task region-strata/M1 with assignees Maya,Ravi,Sam.

ops-bot: Task created: https://tasks.internal/region-strata/M1 — due 8w from 1849999000.

Jesse: customer ask matrix: I'll compile top 5 customers that will benefit from M1 vs ones that need M2. Will share by EOD Friday.

Sam: implementation notes for infra: prefer incremental guardrails — start with soft-routing headers + metrics, then add strict enforcement in M2. avoid heavy migrations.

Maya: action items summarized: 
- Jesse: customer matrix (due Fri)
- Sam + Ravi: draft DSL sketch + rollback plan (next Tue)
- Lina: acceptance rubric doc for GTM (next Wed)
- Maya: consolidate into one PRD and link to repo 

Ravi: minor ask — include failure-mode playbooks per lane (what happens if primary region is unavailable). sample: degrade to lower-cost model, or route to cross-region with warning header.

Maya: good point. I'll add a matrix of degradation strategies.

Lina: :thumbsup: this feels actionable. can we add a simple metric to measure "isolation readiness" (0-100) per tenant? helps sales show progress.

Maya: love that — propose a 5-point checklist that rolls up to isolation readiness %. will draft.

Sam: OK — I'll pair with Maya on infra signals we can compute for that score.

Maya: thanks team. I'll drop the PRD link here once consolidated. If anyone else wants in, ping me.
